metadata.title: Bi, Yang, Marchetti & Manning (2016) Physical Review X 6(2):021011 — Motility-driven glass and jamming transitions in biological tissues: Self-Propelled Voronoi (SPV) reference claims
metadata.citation: Bi D, Yang X, Marchetti MC, Manning ML (2016). Motility-driven glass and jamming transitions in biological tissues. Physical Review X 6(2):021011.
metadata.provenance_note: Equations, parameter conventions and the four headline claims below are taken from the published text/abstract of Bi et al. (2016) as recalled offline (no network access during Pass 3); the single figure-derived number (approximate_boundary_slope_alpha_dr1) is an approximate reading of Fig. 1(a) and is flagged as such with an explicit uncertainty. Any field marked approximate must not be treated as digitised data.

spv_model_definition.energy: E = sum_i [ K_A (A_i - A_0)^2 + K_P (P_i - P_0)^2 ]  (Eq. 1; cells are Voronoi polygons of the cell centers r_i; no 1/2 prefactor)
spv_model_definition.dynamics: dr_i/dt = mu F_i + v_0 n_i,  F_i = -grad_i E,  n_i = (cos theta_i, sin theta_i);  dtheta_i/dt = eta_i(t),  <eta_i(t) eta_j(t')> = 2 D_r delta_ij delta(t - t')  (Eqs. 2-3)
spv_model_definition.units: K_A = K_P = 1, A_0 = 1, mu = 1: lengths in sqrt(A_0), time in 1/(mu K_A A_0); dimensionless target shape index p_0 = P_0 / sqrt(A_0); r = K_P/(K_A A_0) = 1
spv_model_definition.effective_diffusivity: D_eff = D_s / D_0,  D_s = lim_{t->inf} <|Delta r(t)|^2> / (4 t),  D_0 = v_0^2 / (2 D_r) (free active-Brownian diffusivity)
spv_model_definition.solid_criterion_long_time: D_eff < 1e-3 (Bi et al. 2016 Fig. 1; requires long-time steady-state MSD)

bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.zero_motility_glass_point_note: At v_0 -> 0 the SPV glass transition line meets the Bi et al. (2015) zero-temperature rigidity transition at p_0 ~= 3.81 (Fig. 1a).
bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.structural_order_parameter_note: The observed cell shape index q = <P_i/sqrt(A_i)> at the glass transition is q_c ~= 3.81 for all (v_0, D_r) studied (Fig. 4): solid for q < 3.81, fluid for q > 3.81.
bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.motility_direction: Increasing self-propulsion speed v_0 lowers p_0^c (the solid region shrinks; motility fluidises the tissue at fixed p_0) (Fig. 1a).
bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.persistence_direction: Decreasing the rotational diffusion D_r (longer persistence time 1/D_r) enlarges the fluid region, i.e. p_0^c decreases as D_r decreases (Fig. 3); equivalently p_0^c increases toward 3.81 as D_r grows.
bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.approximate_boundary_slope_alpha_dr1_not: APPROXIMATE: effective initial slope -dp_0^c/dv_0 of the D_r = 1 boundary in Fig. 1(a), read from the figure from memory; the published boundary is curved and this value is only an order-of-magnitude anchor. Treat as a qualitative check that the simulated slope is positive and O(0.3-1).
bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.minimum_fluid_to_solid_t1_rate_contrast_: Expectation (not a published number): across the glass boundary the neighbour-exchange (T1) rate must change by at least an order of magnitude; used as the reference for the fixed-p_0 motility ablation ratio.
bi_2016_spv_glass_transition.minimum_p0c_shift_dr_0p25_to_4_note: Sign-only reference (not a published number): p_0^c(D_r = 4) - p_0^c(D_r = 0.25) must be >= 0 per the persistence_direction claim.

finite_time_estimators_used_by_script.dt_rule: dt = min(0.1, 0.2 / D_r) (overdamped Euler; dt = 0.25 diverges at K_A = 1)
finite_time_estimators_used_by_script.initial_state: uniform random seeds FIRE-minimised at v_0 = 0 to |F|_max < 1e-7 (max 600 steps)
finite_time_estimators_used_by_script.D_s_estimator: slope/4 of the time-origin-averaged MSD over lags tau in [T/8, T/2]
finite_time_estimators_used_by_script.T1_rate_estimator: Delaunay-edge losses per cell per unit time over the second half of the window, sampled every 0.5 time units
finite_time_estimators_used_by_script.fluid_criterion_finite_time: Gamma_T1 / v_0 > 0.02 T1 events per cell per unit free-path length v_0 t (log-interpolated boundary in p_0); the motility normalisation puts slow (small v_0) and fast fluids on the same scale, analogous to D_eff = D_s / D_0. D_eff is reported alongside but its finite-window solid floor (~5e-3) prevents applying Bi's 1e-3 criterion
